today_summary: GCM26 gapped to $4,544.40 (+$124.40, +2.82%) on the heaviest flow of the cycle — 11,500 call contracts against 3,513 puts, a 3.3:1 skew and 2.6× the four-day average call volume. Spot now sits just $34 above the gamma flip at $4,510, where cumulative net GEX crosses from −26.1 to +46.2. The chain stays structurally call-heavy at 195,639 calls vs 68,945 puts (P/C OI 0.35), with the thickest near-money gamma shelf at $4,500–$4,510 (14,615 combined call OI). Today's buying skewed far-OTM: 2,126 contracts at $5,000 and 1,555 at $5,500.
five_day_thesis: The five-day tape was four flat sessions ($4,419.8 → $4,436.6 → $4,473.0 → $4,420.0) followed by one +$124.40 breakout — the entire +$124.60 weekly gain arrived in a single print. ATM IV compressed −1.22pp (23.22% → 22.00%) through that gap, an unusual vol crush on an upside break that marks the move as spot-chasing rather than premium-bidding. The long-gamma window thickened 36% (gex_total_window 439.2 → 598.9) and the flip strike ratcheted up from roughly $3,540 to $4,510, dragging the stabilizing-regime boundary directly underneath spot for the first time this cycle. Max pain has held $6,200 for four straight sessions (down from $6,250) but is inert — it is anchored by 27,562 legacy call contracts at $8,000, not by tradeable near-money OI, so treat it as noise rather than a magnet. The put wall has not moved off $3,500 in five sessions, confirming no downside hedge has been rebuilt anywhere between $4,300 and spot.

prediction: Bias bullish while $4,510 holds.
